sentences.text:
Order 
Petitioners have filed this petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India challenging orders dated 21/03/2025 passed in RCMS No.352/2024-25 and award dated 06/07/2021.
2.
Counsel appearing for petitioners submitted that respondent No.5 wants to do mining over the land of petitioners, for which he has sought permission and compensation has also been determined by SDO.
Compensation has also been deposited.
Petitioners are not satisfied with the compensation amount.

As per provisions of Section 247(4) of M. P. Land Revenue Code, 1959 if rights of owner has been infringed or disturbance of surface of such land, then SDO shall determine the compensation in accordance with provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and if a person is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17261 2 WP-12218-2025 not satisfied with said award, then he may approach the Civil Court in accordance with provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 [new Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'Act of 2013')].
It is submitted that he may be permitted to file reference under Section 64 of Act of 2013 against an award passed by SDO.
Counsel for petitioner relied upon order dated 27/01/2023 passed in W.P. No.10628/2018.

Relevant part of order is quoted as under :-

sentences.text: Rights over minerals is vested in State Government under Section 57 of M.P. Land Revenue Code.
As per Section 57, all lands belong to State Government and State is owner of mines, quarries, minerals and all rights in sub-soil of land.
Said rights are property of State Government.
It has been held by Division Bench of this Court in case of Shyam Bihari Singh (supra) that State is owner of minerals which is lying beneath the land even if the land is private land.

State can grant mining lease to any person in accordance with the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation)
Act, 1957 and Mineral Concession Rules, 1960.

entities.text:
Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation)
Act, 1957
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Consent of private owner of land is not required while granting lease.

Since rights of owners of land in question is infringed by occupation or by disturbance of surface of land therefore, Section 247(4)
is enacted, by which S.D.O. has to grant adequate compensation to the owners of land in question in accordance with the Land Acquisition Act.
Adequacy of the said award can be challenged before the Civil Court.

Compensation to be granted under this Section is one time compensation and it has not been laid down in Section 247 of M.P. Land Revenue Code that second exercise of determination of compensation will again be taken after expiry of lease.
Petitioner is owner of land in question and he has been granted compensation for use of minerals in said land.
Land is to be used by lessee for mining of minerals on surface or beneath it.
Lessee cannot claim any title over the land in question."

3. Learned senior counsel appearing for respondent No.5 submitted that compensation amount as determined by SDO has already been deposited, therefore, respondent No.5 may be permitted to excavate the minerals from the land and his possession may not be NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17261 3 WP-12218-2025 disturbed by petitioners.
If petitioners want to file an application for enhancement of compensation, they may do so.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
5.

Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, Writ Petition is disposed off granting liberty to petitioners to file an application under Section 64 of Act of 2013 for raising all their objections regarding compensation awarded to them.
If petitioners file such an application, then said application be considered by Civil Court after giving notice to respondent No.5.
Evidence be taken and thereafter final order be passed in reference.

6. Cost of Rs.2,50,000/- is imposed on respondent No.5 as averment was made that Appeal will lie before Commissioner, though as per provisions of Section 247(4) of M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959 petitioners ought to have been given liberty to approach Civil Court in accordance with provisions of Act of 2013.
There was delay in determination of compensation amount as petitioners went in Appeal before Commissioner against order of SDO.
Proper assistance was not given in case by respondent No.5.
Cost of Rs.2,50,000/- be paid to petitioners.
7. With the aforesaid direction, Writ Petition is disposed off.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE as Balmik Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133726609/
